The test image shows a corn stalk with a dark black/brown lesion at a node area — wet-looking, necrotic tissue with clear dark discoloration. This points to a stalk rot disease. Top candidates: Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot.

Now I'll view one reference from each top candidate class.

I've used 7 views (1 test + 6 references). One view remaining. The test image shows a green stalk with a distinct dark black/purple lesion at the node — wet-looking. Anthracnose can cause dark stalk node lesions. Let me check it.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Green corn stalk, close-up at a node. Leaf sheath peeled back revealing a distinct dark black/purple lesion concentrated at the node. Tissue looks wet and necrotic.

- **Anthracnose (Corn_Disease_10.jpg)**: Shows stalks with dark black discoloration specifically at the nodes — this is the closest visual match. The node-specific black lesion pattern is characteristic of Anthracnose stalk rot.

- **Physoderma_Stalk_Rot (17.jpg)**: Scattered small black dots across the stalk surface — different pattern, not the solid node lesion seen in the test.

- **Bacterial_Stalk_Rot**: Shows wilted/dead leaves, whole-plant symptoms — does not match the localized node lesion.

- **Charcoal/Diplodia Stalk Rot**: Internal cross-section views or dry tan discoloration — neither matches the black, wet node lesion.

The dark black lesion localized at the node on an otherwise green stalk is the hallmark of Anthracnose stalk rot.
